output.summary: A small deciduous tree native to East Asia, including Korea, China and Japan, kousa dogwood has showy whitish bracts that may fade red and sweet pink-to-red berries. The berry pulp is eaten raw, while the tough, bitter rind is usually discarded; the fruit is sometimes made into wine, and young leaves can be cooked and eaten.
output.edibilityNote: Berry pulp is eaten raw; the edible but tough, bitter rind is usually discarded. Fruit is sometimes made into wine, and young leaves are cooked.
